_source: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise (https://attack.mitre.org/). Descriptions are short paraphrases written for this project; consult the ATT&CK site for authoritative text.

T1486.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
T1486.summary: Adversary encrypts files on endpoints or shares to make data unavailable, usually followed by a ransom demand.

T1490.name: Inhibit System Recovery
T1490.summary: Adversary deletes shadow copies, backup catalogs or disables boot recovery so the victim cannot restore without paying.

T1489.name: Service Stop
T1489.summary: Adversary stops services such as databases, mail or backup agents, often to release file locks before encryption.
mitigations: M1022 Restrict File and Directory Permissions

T1562.001.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
T1562.001.summary: Adversary disables or tampers with antivirus, EDR or logging so later actions are not blocked or recorded.
mitigations: M1022 Restrict File and Directory Permissions

T1134.name: Access Token Manipulation
T1134.summary: Adversary abuses tokens or sensitive privileges (e.g. SeDebugPrivilege) to act with higher rights.

T1068.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
T1068.summary: Adversary exploits a software weakness to gain elevated execution, e.g. a dropped binary running as SYSTEM.

T1059.001.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1059.001.summary: Adversary uses PowerShell, often with encoded or hidden command lines, to download and run payloads.
mitigations: M1042 Disable or Remove Feature or Program

T1027.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
T1027.summary: Adversary hides commands or payloads, e.g. Base64-encoded PowerShell, to evade inspection.

T1204.002.name: User Execution: Malicious File
T1204.002.summary: A user opens a malicious document whose macro or exploit spawns a script interpreter.

T1083.name: File and Directory Discovery
T1083.summary: Adversary enumerates files, folders and shares to find data worth encrypting or stealing.

T1135.name: Network Share Discovery
T1135.summary: Adversary lists network shares (net view / net share) to spread encryption beyond the first host.

T1482.name: Domain Trust Discovery
T1482.summary: Adversary queries domain trusts (e.g. nltest) to plan lateral movement.
